newsitem.title: UK: OPEC Feb output climbs to 26.77 mbpd - Reuter surv.
newsitem.headline: OPEC Feb output climbs to 26.77 mbpd - Reuter surv.

text.p: OPEC kept its foot on the accelerator in February pushing production higher again despite signals from world oil markets that prices are more vulnerable than for a number of months.

Crude oil production from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries rose 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.77 million in February from 26.64 million in January, a survey by Reuters of OPEC officials, oil companies and analysts found.

Official OPEC output quotas, a combined 25.033 million bpd for the 11-member cartel, remain an historical irrelevance for all but one or two core Gulf member countries led by Saudi Arabia. Output has risen 730,000 bpd in the past three months.
"OPEC no longer reacts to price changes," said oil analyst Geoff Pyne at finance house UBS. "A production-cutting response to weaker prices is unlikely."

"When the market was able to absorb everything thrown at it, it didn't matter. But if prices come off much more then OPEC overproduction will become an issue for the market again," said an OPEC member country official.

Iraq's second full month of exports under the U.N.'s oil-for-food exchange saw Baghdad selling just over 500,000 bpd on top of its domestic consumption for a total 1.15 million, little changed from January.

Efforts to raise exports amid falling crude prices to meet the United Nations' permitted billion-dollar target by March 9, for sales in the first 90 days of the scheme, appear not to have kicked in during February.

Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has found difficulty raising sales sufficiently under the cumbersome and increasingly uncompetitive pricing formula for exports of its Kirkuk and Basrah light crudes.

But monitors said extra shipments slated for early March appeared to have boosted exports significantly. Sales would have to run at some 750,000 bpd in the first nine days of March to hit the billion dollar target, analysts estimate.
Several OPEC members posted an upward creep in supplies in February while maintenance kept a lid on others.
Nigeria ticked up to 2.15 million bpd, 285,000 bpd over quota, aided by rising flows from two or three long-term joint-venture producers and the recently commissioned NGO field.
OPEC's champion quota violator Venezuela managed to push production higher despite a drastic slump in spot sour crude values on the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Caracas added 10,000 bpd for 3.18 million bpd in February to stay on track for its targetted 3.42 million on average for the year.
OPEC's trio of Gulf producers all were seen running above quota, but by relatively small volumes.

The UAE advanced to 2.28 million bpd as a result of an increase at its Upper Zakum field. Kuwait moved to 2.09 million. Preliminary estimates for OPEC's biggest producer Saudi Arabia put the kingdom at 8.05 million.
Slightly lower figures were returned by Libya, Indonesia and Algeria in February.
The Reuter survey seeks a best estimate of wellhead flows in OPEC countries based on the views of officials, industry monitors and analysts inside and outside member countries.
OPEC quotas are based on supply to market, defined to exclude movements to, but not sales from storage.
